# CMU 15-445/645: Intro to Database Systems

> > Carnegie Mellon University's comprehensive database systems course covering SQL, ACID transactions, storage engines, and hands-on implementation through the BusTub DBMS project.

This course, taught by Andy Pavlo, Jignesh Patel, and others at CMU's School of Computer Science, provides both undergraduate (15-445) and graduate (15-645) level instruction in database internals. Students implement core database components in C++ including buffer pool managers, B+Trees, and query execution engines using the BusTub educational database system.

## Key Topics

- Database Systems
- SQL
- BusTub DBMS
- C++ Implementation
- Buffer Pool Management
- B+Tree Indexing
- ACID Transactions
- Query Execution
- Storage Engines
- Database Internals
- CMU 15-445/645
- Andy Pavlo
- Gradescope
- ARC Replacement Policy

## Projects & Homework

- [Homework #1 - SQL](https://15445.courses.cs.cmu.edu/spring2026/homework1): SQL queries using MusicBrainz dataset with SQLite and DuckDB
- [Project #0 - C++ Primer](https://15445.courses.cs.cmu.edu/spring2026/project0): C++17 primer project for BusTub DBMS prerequisite assessment
- [Project #1 - Buffer Pool Manager](https://15445.courses.cs.cmu.edu/spring2026/project1): Implement buffer pool manager with ARC replacement policy in BusTub
